title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Three ingredients, one emulsion. The technique recipe.
source: Sample recipe — replace with the real version from a starred chat

items.note: for the pasta water — go light, the cheese is salty

steps.text: Toast the cracked pepper in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute.
steps.why: Heat blooms the pepper's fat-soluble aromatics so they infuse the sauce instead of sitting on top of it.

steps.text: Boil the pasta in shallow, lightly salted water — you want it starchy. Pull it 2 minutes shy of the package time.
steps.why: Shallow water concentrates the starch the pasta sheds, and that starchy water is the backbone of the emulsion — it IS the sauce.

steps.text: While it boils: mash the pecorino with a ladle of cooled pasta water into a thick paste. This is the emulsion base — no clumps.
Transfer pasta to the pepper pan with a splash of pasta water and finish cooking over low heat, tossing.
Kill the heat. Wait 30 seconds. Add the pecorino paste and toss hard until glossy, loosening with pasta water a spoon at a time.
steps.why: Above about 150°F pecorino's proteins seize into strings. The pause plus the starch coating lets the cheese melt into an emulsion instead of clumping.

plating: Twirl into a tight nest with tongs, pour any pan sauce over, dust with pecorino and one more crack of pepper.
elevations: Lemon zest over the top just before serving — cuts the salt and fat.
Fry a handful of coarse breadcrumbs in olive oil and shower them over for crunch.
variations: Add 1 tbsp butter with the cheese paste for training wheels — more stable emulsion, slightly less sharp.
